scope: Primary sources checked for a small set of cultural and historical motifs. The adventure worlds, dialogue, people, conflicts, travel geography, and solutions are original fiction. Source references do not imply endorsement.

sources.title: The Persian Garden
sources.notes: UNESCO describes nine Iranian gardens and the importance of four-part layouts, water, plants, and architecture. This informs the fictional garden paths and the respect shown to their keepers.
sources.limits: The invented courtyard and water problem are not accounts of an actual site. Iran is culturally and geographically diverse; this motif cannot represent every Iranian life.

sources.title: About the Silk Roads
sources.notes: UNESCO describes connected land and maritime networks that carried goods, skills, ideas, and cultural exchanges. This supports the anthology’s emphasis on introductions, shared books, caravans, and sea travel.
sources.limits: Rook’s sequence of journeys is invented and deliberately mixes technologies. It is neither a historical itinerary nor a current travel recommendation.

sources.title: Traditional design and practices for building Chinese wooden arch bridges
sources.notes: UNESCO identifies bridge-making knowledge associated with communities in Fujian and Zhejiang, including craftsmanship and continuing transmission of skills. The fictional apprentice and teacher show a living craft rather than a frozen historical scene.
sources.limits: The story is not a construction manual. Its bridge, repair, crew, and records are invented, and one regional tradition is not a claim about all Chinese communities.

sources.title: Kizhi Pogost
sources.notes: UNESCO documents a Karelian architectural ensemble on Lake Onega and the significance of its wooden buildings and carpentry. The story borrows only the broad idea of caring for skilled timber architecture.
sources.limits: The fictional community hall is not Kizhi, and the chapter does not reproduce sacred architecture or suggest visitors can attempt specialist work. A single winter community is not all of Russia.

sources.title: Колобок — Русские сказки и былины
sources.organization: Lomonosov Moscow State University, Institute of Russian Language and Culture educational project
sources.notes: The university’s educational edition presents a traveling round-loaf folktale. Bun is an original talking-loaf character with a different plot, new dialogue, and an ending he chooses for himself.
sources.limits: No text, refrain, illustration, or recording from this edition is reused. Bun’s adventure is an original nod to a folktale motif, not a faithful retelling or claim that the motif belongs to one country alone.

sources.title: The Bill of Rights: A Transcription
sources.notes: The National Archives supplies the original text of the first ten amendments, including the Second Amendment, and explains their ratification. The chapter’s display and missing-page correction are fictional; the source is provided for actual document reading.
sources.limits: The chapter identifies subjects, not present-day legal scope or interpretation. It offers no weapons instruction, jurisdiction advice, partisan endorsement, or legal verdict. Rights are approached through accurate source access and room for discussion.
